headline: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra scored 62.7% on a hard reasoning test under neutral conditions, far below the 99.9% OpenAI highlighted using a setup only it can run.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 1: the launch dates from 3 Sep 2026 and the debate is about how to read figures already published.
importance_line: Anyone comparing AI models should treat the 62.7% as the like-for-like figure, since no rival can reproduce the 99.9%, though ARC Prize's own leader called the jump a major step.
summary: Startup Fortune reports, citing the ARC Prize Foundation's published results, that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra scored 62.7% on ARC-AGI-3, a test of reasoning in unfamiliar interactive games, under ARC Prize's standard neutral setup. OpenAI's own chart showed 99.9% using a special adapter that carries the model's reasoning state between turns and that no other lab has access to, so the two numbers are not comparable; ARC Prize founder François Chollet praised the result but stressed he was not claiming it means AGI, or human-level general intelligence.
notes: Launch 3 Sep 2026; coverage of ARC Prize results on 4 Oct.
